title: MIDEA kicks off Xpress Hub tour with space and money saving appliances
summary: As a southie, I really make it a point to make my trips up north worth the drive. After discovering the MIDEA Xpress Hub was unveiling its new product line at Waltermart in North EDSA, I had to see…

blocks.text: As a southie, I really make it a point to make my trips up north worth the drive. After discovering the MIDEA Xpress Hub was unveiling its new product line at Waltermart in North EDSA, I had to see for myself what new things MIDEA had to unveil. I say this as a MIDEA customer, having two aircons, and one smart refrigerator installed just last year.

One thing I learned is that MIDEA is quite deliberate with their product releases. I’ve seen their booths at IFA in Berlin for two consecutive years. On one end, they’ve focused on AI and the smart home – my refrigerator notifies me if the kids leave the door open! But this time, the Xpress Hub had other things to offer. In this economy, many families are on save mode. It doesn’t necessarily mean they are consuming less — it has more to do with making smarter decisions to save where it counts. There were three products I found super interesting: a low-smoke griddle, the XpressFlame gas range, and the fully electric stovetop range and oven.

Consider the Midea XpressFlame gas range. Midea engineered an advanced burner system that is 10% more efficient than standard burners. On paper, 10% looks like a modest, incremental saving, but when that adds up, it becomes equivalent to saving one tank of gas per year. That’s pretty huge given the price of gas and oil in this economy.

The XpressFlame achieves the saving with the way the burner is designed. The heat is released in a vortex-like flame with wider slits that is more akin to Asian cooking. Apparently most gas ranges are designed for the western market and the wider slits work better for cooking things like fried rice, stir fry, and other Asian dishes.

Then there is the Midea Low-Smoke Griddle. Indoor grilling is historically a compromise. If you want that deep, high-heat sear on a piece of meat, you usually have to accept the inevitable tax: a smoke-filled living room, greasy residue settling on your furniture, and your clothes smelling like a barbecue joint for the next twelve hours. In an enclosed home, that smell will last the entire evening till the next morning.

This griddle tackles those pain points through two specific engineering choices. First, it uses graphene infrared heating that reaches cooking temperature in a mere 0.2 seconds. There is no tedious pre-heating cycle where energy is wasted heating up an empty plate. Second, the built-in Smoke Guard technology directs oils and drippings away from the heating elements before they can burn and vaporize into blue smoke. The entire bottom is a catch basin that you need to fill with water. This is where the oils dissipate so smoke doesn’t rise and it also acts as a secondary heating element from the bottom of the grill.

To be clear, this product is built for the urban professional living in a tightly sealed condo who wants a steak on a Tuesday evening without triggering the building’s smoke alarms. It’s meant for the family that wants a simple and fun way to grill at the dinner table without the hassles of smoking and charring.

The third piece of the puzzle is the Midea 50cm All-Electric Range. If you live in a suburban home with a massive open-concept kitchen, appliance dimensions rarely cross your mind. But for those navigating dense city apartments, space is the ultimate luxury.

A 50cm footprint means you are reclaiming valuable physical territory in your kitchen layout. Instead of relying on a mismatched array of single-burner portable stoves cluttering your countertops, this range consolidates four independent ceramic cooking zones and a spacious oven into a single, compact profile. The smooth ceramic glass surface also removes the physical dread of cleanup—a quick wipe down replaces the tedious scrub-and-soak routine required by traditional iron grates.
If you’re an aspiring home baker, the precision oven allows you to bake pastries that are more sensitive to temperature.
As an added bonus, if you’re running off-grid power like solar panels, your electricity costs for cooking can actually be zero!

Seeing these releases made me realize that while high-concept smart home concepts make for great press releases at European trade shows, pragmatic, localized engineering is what actually makes the daily quality of life in a Filipino home simply ideal.
Whether it is reclaiming an extra month of cooking gas or grilling indoors without the lingering odor of smoke, it’s all about the way tech works for you and for your home.
The Midea Xpress Hub tour will be making its next destination this coming October 29 to November 2 at Abenson Waltermart Sucat Road.
